issue.mint_text: Royal Mint (United Kingdom); no mint mark on this issue

new.story: Ten cents from the East Caribbean States, dated 1991 — an older brother to the 2014 steel ten cents filed the same day. The back is the same Golden Hind, Drake's little round-the-world galleon, with a 10 on each side. The front is what gives its age away: the Queen is young here, in Arnold Machin's portrait wearing a tiara, the likeness these islands used from the 1980s into the early 2000s before switching to the older crowned portrait. Eight Caribbean islands spend this one money, and coins like this crossed between them in every ferry and market stall. This one is copper-nickel, from the British Royal Mint years, heavier in the hand than the steel strikes that replaced it.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Reverse: EAST CARIBBEAN STATES around the Golden Hind, the date 1991 down the right rim read digit by digit in an enlarged view (1-9-9-1), a 10 on each side of the ship, TEN CENTS below. Obverse: QUEEN ELIZABETH THE SECOND around the young Machin portrait — a different portrait generation from the collection's 2004 strikes of this denomination, which carry the crowned Rank-Broadley portrait, and from the 2014 steel strike filed beside it; that portrait is what places this coin in the 1989-2000 striking of the design. Filed as its own type (EC.X.10-cents.2) to keep the portrait generations apart, following the collection's existing .2 pattern for second types of a denomination.
